The Ministry of Defence is working with a new partner on its Respect the Range campaign, which raises awareness of safe and responsible access to training areas.
Members of the Trail Riders Fellowship join training safety staff on Salisbury Plain Training Area (Crown Copyright)
The department has collaborated with The Trail Riders Fellowship (TRF) to promote safe access to Salisbury Plain Training Area (SPTA), one of the UK’s most important military training environments.
The campaign features a series of social media videos highlighting the importance of military training, environmental protection and public safety.
The videos focus on the primary purpose of Salisbury Plain Training Area as a military training estate, demonstrating the scale, intensity and complexity of the activity undertaken to prepare Armed Forces personnel for operations. It also highlights the impact that interruptions from members of the public can have on military readiness and training delivery.
Through the collaboration, the TRF provides a great example of how parts of the estate can be accessed responsibly, showcasing how its members engage with the training area safely and underlining the importance of safety awareness, compliance and personal responsibility.
In addition, the videos highlight the nationally important ecology of Salisbury Plain Training Area, including protected habitats and wildlife that are negatively impacted by irresponsible access, often resulting in irreversible damage to flora and fauna.
Lt Col Jamie Powell, Senior Training Safety Officer SPTA, said:
Salisbury Plain Training Area plays a vital role in preparing our Armed Forces for operations and deployment; training that can be many months in the planning. Every time training is interrupted it creates delay, additional costs and potentially results in vital training being missed.
By working with responsible user groups such as the Trail Riders Fellowship, we’re able to demonstrate that safe and responsible public access can be achieved whilst respecting the land’s primary military use.
Our members value continued access to Salisbury Plain Training Area and recognise the importance of respecting its military purpose. We’re pleased to support this campaign and help promote safe, responsible use of the training estate.
